In the middle circle, write first the name of the hour in which you perform the work; in the second place, the name of the Angel of the hour; third, the seal of the Angel of the hour; fourth, the name of the Angel who presides over that day in which you perform the work, and the names of his ministers; fifth, the name of the present season; sixth, the name of the Spirits reigning in that part of the season and presiding over it; seventh, the name of the head of the zodiac sign reigning in that part of the season in which you perform the work; eighth, the name of the Earth according to that part of the season in which you perform the work; ninth, and to complete the middle circle, write the names of the Sun and Moon according to the aforementioned calculation of time. For when the season is changed, the names also change.

In the outer circle, let there be assigned in the four corners the names of the angels presiding over the air on that day when you perform the work, namely the King and his three ministers. Outside the circle, in the four corners, let there be pentagons <note>likely referring to five-pointed stars or pentagrams used as protective symbols</note>.
